Commentary.Commentary: We are back for England's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Phil Salt and Will Jacks are the two openers for England. Matthew Forde will start with the new ball for West Indies. A slip in place. Away we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

As many as 9 bowling options including himself were used by Livingstone but as a unit, they could not limit the damage in a fashion they would have liked. Only 16 runs were scored in the 3 overs before the 50th over and a good last over could have helped the tourists to take a bit of momentum into their batting effort but it wasn't to be. A ray of hope for England is that the last 6 games at this venue have been won by the chasing side but given the lack of experience in their batting unit, this is a pretty tall ask. A good Powerplay will set them up nicely for the rest of the chase. Back in a bit for the second half of the game.

Keacy Carty is down for a chat. He says it looks like a good total and the batting group did pretty well and they will now look to defend it. Adds that they played well despite losing a couple of quick wickets and he kept things simple and put the bad balls away. Appreciates the skipper for the way he led from the front and says Hope is a wonderful player and the whole world knows it.

Both reached well-earned fifties and their 143-run stand well and truly set a platform for a big total. Sherfane Rutherford capitalised on the groundwork laid by Hope and Carty and got off the blocks quickly. His 36-ball 54 and a quickfire cameo from Hetmyer kept the momentum going for the hosts. Dropped when he was on 60 by Salt, Hope made the most of that life as he went on to score his 17th ODI ton. After reaching the landmark, he shifted gears and after his departure, Forde did what was asked of him with his 11-ball 23 propelling West Indies past 325.

Matthew Forde has polished off the innings with his finishing touches! 19 runs off the last over allow West Indies to finish on a high and end up with 328 on the board. Earlier in the game, after being inserted into bat, the hosts were dealt early blows by John Turner. Having lost both openers inside the first four overs, Shai Hope and Keacy Carty dug the hosts out of trouble with a steady partnership. Hope was proactive from the outset, while Carty grew in confidence as he settled in.

A dot to end the inning! An anticlimactic end but West Indies finish on a high at 328/6! Saqib Mahmood spears a wide yorker, outside off, Matthew Forde looks to reach for it but misses. Phil Salt does well to collect it quickly and not allow the batters to steal a run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to commence. The umpires make their way out to the middle and are followed closely by the England players who are spreading out across the field. Evin Lewis and Brandon King are the openers striding out for West Indies. Jofra Archer has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings for England! Away we go!

John Turner is down for a quick chat. He says there was pressure and nerves while making his debut in the last game but those were good. Talks about being around England's side on the last tour and says it was special to see how they train and how small the margins for errors were. Talks about the previous year with him being around the team while studying in his room for his exams and it now feels good with his complete focus on cricket. Concludes that it is very special to be bowling with Jofra Archer who has achieved so much and keeps it all cool.

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani is near the deck. He says that there was some rain around overnight but the skies look clear right now. Proceeds to tell about the boundary dimensions - the square boundaries are equidistant - 63 metres each with the straight boundary being 73 metres. Carlos Brathwaite joins him and says there is a little bit of moisture and it will be challenging for West Indies up front. Mentions that it will be important for the pacers to hit the 6-8 metre lengths. Ends by saying that it will be crucial for the fast bowlers to be disciplined and for the spinners to control their pace.

Matthew Forde is down for a quick chat. He says he is happy with how he has bowled up front and how things have turned out for him. Talks about Jayden Seales and says they are best mates and to share the attack with him is special. Mentions how important it is for him to adapt to the conditions and with this surface offering nice carry and bounce he looks to use his cutters and get it right. Talks about his journey from domestic cricket to the international stage and mentions how opportunities present themselves and he had to be ready for it. Concludes that they are one up in the series and will hopefully play well and get another win.

Shai Hope, the skipper of West Indies says that they will need to assess the conditions quickly. Mentions that Shamar Joseph will make his debut while Alzarri Joseph misses out. Talks about the inexperience in their pace attack and says that the youngsters will be eager to grab the opportunity and do well. Concludes that they can't look too far ahead and they have to just try and play good cricket every time they go out and they will be looking to keep up the consistency which will be the key.

The captain of England, Liam Livingstone says that there was a bit of rain around last night and they want to make use of the moisture. Feels that they did not bowl badly in the first game and lauds Jofra Archer and John Turner for the way they bowled. Hopes that the spinners can get some assistance in the middle phase from this surface. Reckons that as a batter, it is important that you play your natural game and find the way that works for you in ODI cricket. Further says that many batters got starts in the last game and hopes they can make it big, once they get in. Informs that they have made one change with Saqib Mahmood coming in for Jamie Overton.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Evin Lewis, Keacy Carty, Shai Hope (C/WK), Shimron Hetmyer, Sherfane Rutherford, Roston Chase, Gudakesh Motie, Matthew Forde, Jayden Seales, Shamar Joseph (On ODI debut) (In for Alzarri Joseph).
TOSS - England have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

A couple of rain delays shortened the West Indies innings to 35 overs in the first game and rain could be a factor again today, as intermittent showers are expected during the game. Let’s hope the weather doesn’t play spoilsport and we get a full game in. Stay tuned for the toss and team news!

England, meanwhile, brought in four debutants for the first ODI, and their lack of experience showed as they struggled to adapt in a heavy defeat. Their batting unit faltered, managing only 209 runs after being inserted into bat. To keep the series alive, Liam Livingstone and Co. will need a much-improved showing, not only in their batting but across all departments, with a focus on executing well as a cohesive unit.

The hosts were flawless in the series opener, securing a well-deserved lead. A commanding bowling performance set up their victory, and Evin Lewis's entertaining knock took them comfortably over the line. After a disappointing tour of Sri Lanka, where they lost both the T20I and ODI series, Shai Hope and his men will be hungry to taste the success of a series win here.

With West Indies leading the series 1-0, they will be looking to seal the series today, while England seek a quick turnaround to force the decider.
